answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 38% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the nectar calculation reruns each epoch, the copper weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the shale settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 96 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 28 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
